Jain philosophical treatise 'Samayasara' was authored by?
x:
Samayasara is one of the most important philosophical works of Digambara Jainism, written by the great Jain philosopher Acharya Kundakunda (Kundakundacharya). The text explains the true nature of the soul (Jiva) and emphasizes the distinction between the eternal soul and the material body. It teaches that liberation (Moksha) can be attained through self-realization, right knowledge and detachment from worldly desires. Samayasara continues to be regarded as one of the foundational texts of Digambara Jain philosophy and has been translated into several Indian languages.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).

s: Who has the title "Syadvadachala Simha"?
x:
Somadeva Suri, the famous Jain scholar, bore the title "Syadvadachala Simha" for his mastery over the Syadvada philosophy of Jainism. He authored important works such as Yasastilaka Champu and Nitivakyamrita, which occupy an important place in Jain literature.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).

s: Who preached the "Syadvada" philosophical tradition?
x:
Syadvada is one of the fundamental doctrines of Jain philosophy, explaining the theory of conditional predication and the relativity of truth. Among the given options, Acharya Kundakundacharya is the correct answer. He was one of the greatest Digambara Jain philosophers and authored works such as Samayasara, Pravachanasara and Panchastikaya.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (4).
